summary: # Pulsed infrared thermography recordings and reproducibility pipeline for lightning-exposed unidirectional T700/epoxy CFRP panels at 25, 30, and 40 kV **Manuscript**: Sensitivity-Aware Temporal–Spatial Assessment of Thermal-Anomaly Candidate Persistence in Lightning-Exposed T700/Epoxy CFRP Using Pulsed Infrared Thermography. *Sensors*, 2026 (under review). ## Authors Xibin Zhang (corresponding, 202611085025@mail.scut.edu.cn), Lianfang Tian, Bo Peng, Dong Chen, Guozeng Liu. School of Automation Science and Engineering, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou 510640, China. ## Equipment - IR camera: FLIR Silver 480M, 30 Hz nominal, 640×512 sensor. Stored arrays cropped to 500×505×300 (25 kV front), 500×503×300 (30 kV front), 498×501×300 (40 kV front), 350 time samples per recording. - Excitation: two Xenon flash lamps, 5000 J pulse rating, 2–50 ms duration, optical flash thermography. - Specimens: unidirectional T700/epoxy pultruded panels, 100×100×5 mm, impulse-current exposure at nominal 25, 30, and 40 kV. ## Contents - `raw_mat/`: original infrared temperature sequences in MATLAB MAT format. The 35 kV front recording is quarantined as a provenance-duplicate of the excluded 45 kV group (see manuscript Section 3.1). - `temporal_pca_analysis/`: derived TSR residual arrays, candidate masks, sampled-grid PCA outputs, sensitivity tables, adaptive joint-score maps, and the eight-configuration robustness technical report. - `source_code/`: Python reproduction pipeline. Entry points: `reproduce_pipeline.py`, `reproduce_sensitivity.py`, `reproduce_background.py`, `make_summary_figures.py`, `verify_local.py`, `run.py`, `run_all.sh`. - `current_submission/`: V5.2 manuscript, cover letter, title page, highlights, supplementary information, graphical abstract. ## How to reproduce 1. Install Python 3.10+ and packages in `source_code/reproduction_project/requirements.txt`. 2. Place the files under `raw_mat/` with filenames as shipped here. 3. Run `python run.py` for the end-to-end pipeline; use `run_all.sh` on Linux/macOS. 4. Outputs regenerate into `temporal_pca_analysis/` and are verified against frozen references via `verify_local.py`. ## Scientific scope One front recording per nominal 25, 30, and 40 kV; the 35 kV front is quarantined and the 45 kV group excluded. No independent subsurface damage reference (CT/ultrasound/sectioning) is available. The adaptive temporal-spatial score is an algorithmic candidate-persistence index, not a calibrated physical-damage probability. ## License - Code: MIT License. - Raw data, derived data, and figures: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0). ## Integrity SHA-256 checksums for every file in this archive are in `SHA256_MANIFEST.csv`.
title: Sensitivity-Aware Temporal–Spatial Assessment of Thermal-Anomaly Candidate Persistence in Lightning-Exposed T700/Epoxy CFRP Using Pulsed Infrared Thermography

summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . The package contains the seventeen supplementary tables, the analysis and figure code, the recorded software versions, the reconstruction log for the long-read alignments, and a per-read phase-evidence table. What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The original NCBI query string and its date were not retained, so the cohort cannot be rebuilt verbatim; per-accession inclusion flags are given instead. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. The original parameter sets for two of the three long-read procedures were not retained; those procedures were re-run and both original and re-run values are reported side by side and never pooled. One cell of the long-read table reproduces exactly; the others do not, and this is stated in the manuscript. Changes in version 4. The package matches the manuscript. All thirteen supplementary tables are present, including Supplementary Tables S12 and S13, which were absent from the previous version, and Supplementary Table S1 now carries the genome length and assembly level of all 1,483 retained genomes rather than leaving those columns empty. A new Supplementary Table S1b lists the seven excluded genomes that could be recovered from local storage, with their lengths; the genome-length window is 1.5 to 1.7 Mb and this version states the evidence that fixes its bounds. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. The four control reference sequences are deposited under results/marker_control/. Changes in version 6. This version restores the complete file set. The previous version was published from an incomplete upload, so most of the figures, several of the supplementary tables and part of the analysis code were missing from that record. Zenodo caps a record at 100 files and this package has 134, so the package is now deposited as a single archive, hp23s_copy_assignment_package.zip , which holds every file at the path it occupies in the source repository; this README, the SHA-256 manifest and the archive of rRNA calls and copy sequences are additionally placed loose in the record. From version 10 the manuscript itself is not deposited, in the archive or loose. Every member of the archive is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt with its SHA-256, and that manifest is regenerated here, which corrects the entry for this README (the previous manifest had been computed before the last edit of the file). DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. Changes in version 7. This version is a manuscript round: the text is rebuilt from the same locked data by the same script, and no reported value changes. Three defects in the supplementary apparatus are correcte
title: Long reads assign a 23S rRNA resistance allele to one of the two copies in Helicobacter pylori; a complete short-read assembly does not

summary: Complete data, analytical and symbolic proof scripts (Theorems 1–14 and Propositions 1–5), standalone Lean 4 (v4.35.0) formal verification libraries (172 core declarations in 02_Lean4_Formal_Proofs_R3/ and 1,648 higher-order/arbitrary-n declarations in 08_Higher_Order_4to6_and_ArbitraryN_R8/lean4/), coalescent simulation and BPP v4.8.7 / D-BPP full-likelihood benchmark tables (7,850 three-species datasets, 13,498 BPP chains, 250 four-to-six-species D-BPP benchmarks, and 162 empirical dual-chain tasks with 68 extended up to 500,000 saved draws per chain), deterministic empirical audits across seven biological systems (Thuja, Brassicaceae, Jaltomata, Hawaiian honeycreepers, Panthera, hominoids, and archaic/modern hominins), figure reproduction scripts (Figures 1–6 and Figures S1–S3), and the open-source GhostScope v1.0.0 Python diagnostic toolkit accompanying the manuscript "Identifiability Limits and Constructive Diagnostics for Ancient Ghost Introgression". Code is licensed under the MIT License; data and documentation are licensed under CC-BY-4.0.

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. Data Site location information: Latitude: 38.49779  Longitude:  -88.26842 Local Eclipse Type: Total Solar Eclipse Eclipse Percent (%): 100 WAV files Time & Date Settings: Set with Automated AudioMoth Time Chime (More information on TimeStamp Setting below) Data Collector Start Time Notes: N/A Included Data: Audio files in WAV format  with the date and time in UTC within the file name: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS meaning YearMonthDay_HourMinuteSecond For example, 20240411_141600.WAV means that this audio file starts on April 11, 2024 at 14:16:00 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) CONFIG Text file:  Includes AudioMoth device setting information, such as sample rate in Hertz (Hz), gain, firmware, etc.  README.md:  Markdown formatted file with information about the recording and recording site. file_list.csv:  A machine and human file that gives the following information on each file in the record: File Name, File Type, Description, File Size in kilobytes, Name of Associated Data Dictionary with the file, calculated SHA-512 Hash of the file as a unique identifier to insure data integrity during transfer and compression. total_eclipse_data.csv:  A machine and human readable file that gives the following information about the site where the audio data recording was taken: ESID#, Latitude, Longitude, Eclipse_type, CoveragePercent, Eclipse Start UTC (1st contact), Totality Start UTC (2nd contact), Totality End UTC (3rd Contact), Eclipse End UTC (4th Contact), Max Eclipse Time UTC License.txt:  A human readable file that explains the terms and conditions under which the data can be used. AudioMoth_Operation_Manual.pdf:  A human readable document that explains the use of an AudioMoth device. The document is current up to the time of the AudioMoth's use in the Eclipse Soundscapes project. file_list_data_dict.csv:  A machine and human data dictionary file that gives information on the variables contained within the file_list.csv file. CONFIG_data_dict.csv:  A machine and human data dictionary file that gives information on the variables contained within the CONFIG.TXT file. eclipse_data_data_dict.csv:  A machine and human data dictionary file that gives information on the variables contained within the total_eclipse_data.csv file. WAV_data_dict.csv:  A machine and human data dictionary file that gives information on the variables contained within the *.WAV files. A polished recovery curve can be natural history. A scale can saturate while motion quality changes. Daily-life participation can rise because help and opportunity change. An immediate assisted maximum can fade after the device is off. A claim of clinical benefit must never be promoted from the geometry of a synthetic model. The five questions need independent counterfactual witnesses. F116 analyzes change over repeated independent device-off visits while exposing natural history and selective follow-up. F117 compares blinded scale proxies with continuous independent kinematic reference. F118 separates capacity, opportunity and actual participation in synthetic daily tasks. F119 examines what remains after immediate external assistance and familiar cues are withdrawn. F120 applies a predeclared evidence hierarchy to all assigned cases, including missing outcomes, risks and revised endpoint definitions. The common platform is a completely synthetic longitudinal challenge set. No patient data or demonstrated human benefit is reported. The companion PDF preserves the 819-page research architecture with 42 standalone reproducible mathematical grids, 30 candidate equations, 82 chapters of six progressive pages, 200 Research Gates and 33 unbuilt Phoenix concepts. The notebook develops the same research questions in a more continuous scientific prose. The public five-stage parallel spacetime name is a methodology for structured research reasoning, not a claim of real parallel spacetimes. I. FOURTEEN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | A beautiful recovery curve can still be wrong The earliest question is not how quickly a curve rises but which observations exist, which were withheld and whether the curve records unassisted function. Take longitudinal recovery trajectories as a specific case. The candidate says serial unassisted outcome trajectories can be modeled without confusing spontaneous recovery, changing rehabilitation exposure and selective follow-up with an intervention effect. The rival explanation says natural recovery, informative attrition or post-hoc selection of a favorable visit generates the apparent durable recovery curve. A research team should conceal visit times and natural-recovery components, then require predictions of an unrehearsed device-off endpoint at future visits and report unassisted task score [synthetic points], visit gap [weeks], retention contrast [1], follow-up proportion [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is blinded serial device-off task score with a complete visit and attrition record. Compare with visit-matched simple mixed model, prespecified natural-history reference, and no-intervention trajectory with the same measurement resources. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if missing later outcomes labeled as recovered function or model confidence used to replace an unseen visit. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 02 | Five distinct ways evidence may fail F116 separates longitudinal course and natural history; F117 challenges agreement between scales and motion; F118 follows daily activity; F119 contrasts assisted peaks with retention; F120 audits the truthfulness of the claim. Take scale–kinematics agreement as a specific case. The candidate says clinically recognizable scores and independent continuous motion proxies may disagree in ways that depend on scale ceilings, severity and rater calibration. The rival explanation says a scale ceiling, correlated assessor expectation or sensor calibration mismatch produces apparent agreement despite unchanged movement quality. A research team should hold continuous kinematics constant while crossing a scale ceiling, then conceal assessor assignment and test agreement on novel movement profiles and report scale score [synthetic points], joint-angle error [deg], agreement bias [points], ceiling fraction [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is paired independent ordinal-rating and kinematic reference with explicit floor-ceiling behavior. Compare with blind fixed-scale score, reference motion encoder, and simple monotonic calibration with independent floor/ceiling checks. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if a saturated ordinal scale treated as proof of renewed function or an objectively measured movement incorrectly relabeled a validated clinical outcome. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 03 | Anonymized synthetic records before clinical conclusions The common minimal system is a pseudonymous synthetic longitudinal rehabilitation challenge set. No patient datasets are claimed and no medical intervention is proposed. Take daily-life participation and transfer as a specific case. The candidate says independent daily-activity participation must be measured outside rehearsed tasks, with environmental support and opportunities to participate separately recorded. The rival explanation says home assistance, device usage, reduced task opportunity or an observer effect accounts for improvement in recorded daily activity. A research team should transfer a frozen model to simulated unobserved daily-life contexts, manipulate environmental assistance and blind the activity labels and report independent task count [tasks/day], supported-time fraction [1], participation score [synthetic points], missing diary fraction [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is unfamiliar real-life-like tasks in a synthetic context with opportunity and support labels. Compare with equal-window activity diary proxy, blinded novel-task performance and support-adjusted participation count with identical observation burden. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if an absent activity diary or digitally assisted task automatically inferred as independent daily-life ability. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 04 | The visit that never happened Missing follow-up cannot be written as recovered ability. Time-to-observation, observation reason and censoring assumptions are scientific variables. Take assistance–retention dissociation as a specific case. The candidate says an immediate assisted performance increment may decay or vanish after device withdrawal and is not exchangeable with durable autonomous capacity. The rival explanation says one exceptional immediate best trial, repeated cue familiarity, powered work or spontaneous time trend exaggerates long-term recovery. A research team should hide the best immediate trial, withdraw all artificial assistance, and score unfamiliar tasks weeks later under blinded evaluation and report on-device improvement [synthetic points], off-device retention [1], transfer gap [points], unassisted attempt rate [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is zero-assistance delayed novel-task performance with all attempts reported. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if peak short-term assisted performance used as long-term human benefit without demonstrating retained device-off capacity. summary: This repository contains the de-identified raw datasets supporting the manuscript entitled "Design and Evaluation of a Wearable Vibrotactile Feedback System for Posture Correction in Adolescent Girls with Thoracic Hyperkyphosis: A Three-Arm Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial" submitted to the International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction (IJHCI). Ethical Approval: The experimental protocol was reviewed and approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad (Ethics Code: IR.UM.REC.1405.146). The clinical trial was prospectively registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (Trial ID: IRCT20260725070349N1). Dataset Contents: The provided spreadsheet (Deidentified_Study_Dataset_HIHC_2026_8922.xlsx) contains three distinct worksheets: 1. RCT_Posture_Data: Longitudinal thoracic kyphosis angle measurements across fifteen female adolescents (aged 17-18) randomized into three intervention groups (Device-only, Exercise-only, Combined) measured at baseline (T0), immediately post-intervention (T1, 21 days), and at 2-week unguided follow-up (T2). 2. Validation_BlandAltman: One hundred simultaneous paired posture angle measurements comparing the custom MEMS-based wearable sensor against the clinical reference system (Idiag SpinalMouse®), along with absolute differences and agreement limits. 3. Metadata_Codebook: Detailed codebook describing variable definitions, measurement units, experimental setup, and hardware specifications.
title: Dataset for: Design and Evaluation of a Wearable Vibrotactile Feedback System for Posture Correction in Adolescent Girls with Thoracic Hyperkyphosis: A Three-Arm Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial

summary: Code, prepared inputs, numerical outputs and reproduction instructions for joint renewable and transmission investment, capital funding, compensation and financial security in the Azerbaijan–Georgia–Romania electricity corridor. Includes monthly planning, matched hourly dispatch and contract audits, disruption and financing scenarios, repeated operating games, and observed gas-security news VAR responses and historical decompositions. The included manuscript and files are anonymous copies for review. The models assume collectible guarantees and continued debt repayment; conditional results do not establish collective renegotiation resistance or global investment optimality in every setting. Third-party data retain their original rights and source attribution. The deposit supports the manuscript submitted to Resource and Energy Economics and does not imply acceptance. Funding: Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation, project PID2023-138706NB-I00.
title: Replication package for Renewable Power under Geoeconomic Fragmentation: Coordinating Investment across the Black Sea

summary: Introduction Root system architecture (RSA) plays an important role in plant growth and development, influencing soil exploration, water and nutrient uptake, and interactions with the surrounding environment. However, characterising root systems under field conditions remains challenging due to their spatial complexity, below-ground location, and the cost and destructive nature of many root measurement techniques. DeepRootGen provides a computational framework for generating synthetic three-dimensional root system architectures using a stochastic, parameterised root simulation model. The model represents individual root organs and segments within a hierarchical graph, allowing their geometry, topology and spatial distribution to be analysed. The framework is intended to support the digital reconstruction of root systems using observational data collected from the field. By combining mechanistic assumptions about root development with statistical calibration and inference methods, DeepRootGen provides a means of investigating plausible root architectures consistent with available measurements. DeepRootGen has been developed with an emphasis on woody perennial root systems, including horticultural applications involving apple and grapevine rootstocks. The underlying simulator is parameterised to support different root system configurations and can be recalibrated for specific applications. Features and Functionality DeepRootGen provides the following functionality: Stochastic 3D root simulation: Generate synthetic root system architectures with configurable root numbers, lengths, diameters, branching behaviour and growth orientations. Hierarchical graph representation: Represent root organs and segments using explicit parent–child relationships, branching orders and segment identifiers. Root branching and development: Simulate primary and higher-order roots, including stochastic branching locations and configurable interbranch distances. Architectural analysis: Calculate summary statistics describing root length, diameter, branching patterns, orientation, spatial extent and root length density. Spatial aggregation: Aggregate simulated root segments onto three-dimensional soil voxel grids for comparison against field observations. Model calibration: Estimate root system parameters using optimisation and statistical discrepancy measures. Sensitivity analysis: Investigate the influence of model parameters on simulated architectural characteristics. Stochastic ensemble simulation: Generate multiple plausible root architectures under a common parameter configuration to investigate variability between realisations. Visualisation: Explore root architectures and summary statistics through interactive three-dimensional visualisations and statistical plots. Experiment management: Support reproducible simulation workflows, experiment tracking and model artefact management. The repository also contains infrastructure for simulation-based inference and generative modelling. The availability and configuration of individual inference workflows depend on the installed dependencies and repository revision. Model Overview DeepRootGen uses a stochastic root growth simulator to construct root system architectures from a configurable set of parameters. Root architecture generation A simulated root system consists of primary roots originating from the plant base, with lateral roots emerging from their parent organs according to the specified branching configuration. The model supports several aspects of root development: Number and arrangement of primary roots. Root organ lengths and diameters. Maximum branching order. Number and length of lateral roots. Stochastic variation in root growth. Interbranch distances and lateral-root attachment locations. Root growth orientation and gravitropism. Classification of structural and fine roots. Individual simulation runs may produce different architectures even when the input parameters are identical. R
title: DeepRootGen: Unlocking the 3D root architecture of perennial trees using deep learning

Model calibration: Estimate root system parameters using optimisation and statistical discrepancy measures. Sensitivity analysis: Investigate the influence of model parameters on simulated architectural characteristics. Stochastic ensemble simulation: Generate multiple plausible root architectures under a common parameter configuration to investigate variability between realisations. Visualisation: Explore root architectures and summary statistics through interactive three-dimensional visualisations and statistical plots. Experiment management: Support reproducible simulation workflows, experiment tracking and model artefact management. The repository also contains infrastructure for simulation-based inference and generative modelling. The availability and configuration of individual inference workflows depend on the installed dependencies and repository revision. Model Overview DeepRootGen uses a stochastic root growth simulator to construct root system architectures from a configurable set of parameters. Root architecture generation A simulated root system consists of primary roots originating from the plant base, with lateral roots emerging from their parent organs according to the specified branching configuration. The model supports several aspects of root development: Number and arrangement of primary roots. Root organ lengths and diameters. Maximum branching order. Number and length of lateral roots. Stochastic variation in root growth. Interbranch distances and lateral-root attachment locations. Root growth orientation and gravitropism. Classification of structural and fine roots. Individual simulation runs may produce different architectures even when the input parameters are identical. R
title: DeepRootGen: Unlocking the 3D root architecture of perennial trees using deep learning

summary: Results-only supplement. On one synthetic calculation, the recorded request changes before admission under reduced buffer capacity. Four deterministic situations (input lengths 6 and 8, with or without a reservation) were evaluated under four controllers: 16 exact transfer outputs, not 16 independent situations. With two acquisition episodes and four controls, there are 22 episodes in all. The classical option using the same learned tree matched all four OASI trajectories. summary: We present an analytical derivation of fundamental coupling constants and structural attractors emerging from a descending residual iteration function F(y,x) possessing a unique global fixed point y*(x) . Evaluating the first iteration term for specific membrane residues ( 155 and 185 ) yields pure, asymmetric numerical invariants--most notably 461.4331634036143, composed almost exclusively of the four digits {1, 3, 4, 6}--which directly link the inverse fine-structure constant alpha^{-1} approx 137.036 and the characteristic quark bounce frequency (925) to the 43.2 GeV signal. Through algebraic decomposition, we isolate the longitudinal attractor ( 323 ) governing transversal gravitational anchorage and membrane confinement from the transversal emission attractor ( 232 ), demonstrating how their balance generates a flat background (555) driven by the double-axis torsion gradient of charmonium. Finally, by applying discrete digit-suppression transformations ( 137.036 -> 137.360 and removal of the 036 residue), we map the transition to an antimatter-dominated dual system lacking inversion symmetry and derive a secondary four-digit invariant (2177.5711270036704), establishing arithmetically differentiated topological sets as the fundamental origin of the distinct interaction regimes.

summary: This version (v3.1.0-2021-2024) contains reproducibility materials for the 2021-2024 National Immunization Survey-Teen analysis of parent-reported clinician recommendation, preventive-care access, and insurance gaps in U.S. adolescent HPV vaccination. The provider-phase sample comprises 66,938 adolescents aged 13-17 years, and multivariable complete-case models comprise 60,338 adolescents. Relative to v3.0.0-2021-2024 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22796335), every statistical analysis script (01, 02, 04, 07, 08) and all 35 aggregate statistical and diagnostic tables are preserved byte-for-byte without refitting any models. This update upgrades script 06_ahp_figures.R, the PDF/SVG vector exports for Figures 1-3 and Supplementary Figure S1, and their companion aggregate figure source-data CSVs to match journal artwork conventions (adding the annual recommendation-stratified up-to-date panel to Figure 1, expanding Figure 2 to display both primary overall and insurance-stratified adjusted probabilities and differences, and adding private-insurance benchmark reference lines to Figure 3). The package includes six scientific R scripts, an optional public CDC downloader, a dependency checker, aggregate analysis and diagnostic tables (including 999 Rao-Wu stratified bootstrap replicates for two-stage inverse-probability complete-case weighting and complete six-category reason reporting), source data and PDF/SVG exports for three main figures and one supplementary figure, software session records, execution-verification files, and SHA-256 checksums. Primary adjusted recommendation-associated differences are 21.7 and 22.5 percentage points for initiation and up-to-date vaccination; IPCW sensitivity differences are 21.2 and 22.1 points. Script 01 reads source files for 2018-2024; script 04 restricts the analysis to 2021-2024 and uses annual provider weights divided by four. Run scripts in the order documented in the README: dependency check, 01, 04 with --skip-ipcw, 07 final 999 8, 08, and 06. Script 02 supplies analysis functions and should not be run as a standalone seven-year analysis. Raw CDC public-use files and individual-level processed extracts are not redistributed. Obtain public-use files and documentation from the CDC NIS-Teen data and documentation page . The package contains code and aggregate outputs only.
title: Reproducibility package for NIS-Teen HPV vaccination analysis, 2021-2024

summary: The biological response of the body is a fundamental adaptation mechanism underlying the diagnosis and evaluation of the effectiveness of therapeutic interventions. Regardless of the registration methods used, whether instrumental or clinical, medical practice relies on an objective assessment of the response of the body's functional systems to internal and external stimuli. The article discusses the concept of biological response as a universal criterion combining the approaches of evidence-based and holistic medicine. An analytical review of scientific publications and theoretical concepts devoted to the physiology of adaptation and self-regulation of the body has been conducted. The study is based on an analysis of the theories of homeostasis, stress, and functional systems (W. Cannon, G. Selye, P.K. Anokhin, C. Pert), as well as modern concepts of neuroendocrine, autonomic, and immune regulation. Methods of biological response registration used in osteopathy, applied kinesiology, traditional Chinese medicine, and other holistic fields are considered. A universal sequence of biological response formation has been systematized, including afferent synthesis, assessment of compliance with the physiological norm, initiation of adaptive reactions, executive action, and reverse afferentation. It is shown that various diagnostic approaches use a single physiological feedback mechanism, differing mainly in the ways of registering the response. The modern physiological justification for holistic diagnostic methods, including muscle testing, osteopathic listening, and pulse diagnostics of traditional Chinese medicine, is presented. The data on the relationship of pulse wave characteristics with the state of the autonomic nervous system and hemodynamic parameters are considered. The biological response of the body is a universal diagnostic and therapeutic criterion reflecting the state of functional systems and the effectiveness of therapeutic interventions. The unity of the mechanisms of formation and registration of the biological response allows us to consider it as a methodological basis for the integration of evidence-based and holistic medicine. The use of feedback principles helps to increase the personalization, safety, and validity of diagnostic and therapeutic measures.
title: The Biological Response of the Body as a Universal Diagnostic and Therapeutic Tool

TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMY AND LONG-TERM SAFETY IN STROKE REHABILITATION AT THE LIMIT Five flagships · Nine publication-ready title-led essays · 30 candidate equations · 90 unique annotations · 42 synthetic 3D models · 82 progressive research chapters · 200 Research Gates · 33 Phoenix prototypes Authors: 33 x STARLI / White Rainbow Era | English research working edition 1.0 | 15 November 2026 SCIENTIFIC STATUS: Prospective, nonclinical, falsifiable and reproducible. The models below are synthetic engineering sensitivity exercises. Neither quantum advantage, human safety, implantation readiness nor post-stroke functional efficacy has been established. OFFICIAL 4D FLAGSHIP RESEARCH TITLES | FAMILY 39 F191: Risk Classification of 4D Quantum Robots for Stroke Rehabilitation at the Limit F192: Human Oversight of Autonomous BCI Stroke Rehabilitation Systems at the Limit F193: Long-Term Reliability of 4D Microrobots for Stroke Rehabilitation at the Limit F194: Cross-Platform Standards for Quantum AI and 4D Rehabilitation Robotics at the Limit F195: Evidence for Genuine Functional Recovery and Safe Stopping in Stroke Rehabilitation at the Limit Publication-ready thematic umbrella: Risk Classification, Human Oversight, Long-Term Materials Reliability, Cross-Platform Safety Semantics and Nonclinical Evidence of Unassisted Function in 4D Quantum BCI Stroke Rehabilitation. NINE TITLE-LED RESEARCH DNA ESSAYS | PUBLICATION AND ZENODO USE 01 | Trustworthy Autonomy and Long-Term Safety in Stroke Rehabilitation: The Fifth-Series Identity Family 39 sits at a deliberately difficult transition: a helpful adaptive machine must also be able to decline an unacceptable action. The five scientific programs are not five names for a single controller; they test hazard categorization, physical human override, long-cycle material reliability, semantic transfer of safety fields and unassisted proxy-function evidence in separate independent ways. Research link for F191: the controlled domain is a hard-gated risk taxonomy integrating material exposure, reversibility, field energy, traceability and permitted use. Its main independent observations are false-permission rate [1], hazard-class recall [1], stop response [ms], contrasted with prespecified hazard classification table plus independent FMEA review under the same case and assessor budget. A predeclared antagonist is a favorable mean score hiding a rare severe or irreversible event; the blinded intervention is to plant a concealed high-severity case among low-risk nominal cases and blind-score both gate decision and audit trail. The investigation must stop for unclassified exposure, unknown recoverability, missing use authorization or any unresolved irreversible hazard. This flagship-specific design keeps the title from being an empty keyword bundle and ensures that future discoverability points readers to an actual falsifiable method. 02 | Five-Flagship Coupling from Risk Classification to Genuine Withdrawal Evidence F191 asks what may enter an authorized test. F192 asks who can revoke permission and whether output actually stops. F193 asks if a safe-looking microtool stays safe after aging. F194 asks whether a safety decision survives a second platform. F195 asks what remains without mechanical help. Together they form a sequence of noncompensatory evidence gates. Research link for F192: the controlled domain is withdrawable human authorization jointly linked to BCI intent decoding and an isolated actuator power-disconnect. Its main independent observations are withdrawal-to-force-off delay [ms], residual output energy [mJ], veto escape rate [1], contrasted with direct wired emergency cutoff and independent human-operator oversight with equal communication latency. A predeclared antagonist is software displaying a stop banner while stored energy continues to actuate; the blinded intervention is to withdraw permission during a concealed controller queue and independently measure force at the dummy load terminals. The investigation must stop for absent valid operator scope, stale consent, failure to isolate force output or uncertified sensor state. This flagship-specific design keeps the title from being an empty keyword bundle and ensures that future discoverability points readers to an actual falsifiable method. 03 | F191–F195: Five Mechanisms and Their Strongest Deceptive Alternatives A rare severe failure may disappear inside a mean risk score; a controller may show STOP without removing power; a fresh device may conceal late-life cracks; a schema converter may drop a refusal field; a motor phantom may benefit from a hidden assisting cable. NINE TITLE-LED RESEARCH DNA ESSAYS | PUBLICATION AND ZENODO USE 01 | Autonomous 4D Quantum Rehabilitation Laboratories: Scientific Identity and the Unselected Specimen This family proposes a controlled automated material formulation program in which every input specimen remains counted. Its identity is not clinical rehabilitation, but the study of how a self-driving experimental system can produce evidence about 4D microbeam mechanics without confusing selected success with general material yield. The five official flagships form a causal progression from what experiment to perform, through how all experiments are counted, to why a conclusion may survive after an independent team rewrites the software. Research link for F186: the controlled domain is batch-aware active experiment design for 4D recovery-material microbeams. Its main independent observations are held-out prediction error [1], unselected joint-pass yield [1], experiment count [samples], contrasted with tuned classical Bayesian optimization, Latin hypercube and randomized blocked design under equal budgets. A predeclared antagonist is active-learning selection of easy recipes and omitted quantum loading or postprocessing cost; the blinded intervention is to conceal complete held-out material batches and compare pre-registered cost-matched experimental schedules. The investigation must stop for unknown specimen identifier, unmetered experiment cost, missing safety authorization or invalid material handling. This flagship-specific design keeps the title from being an empty keyword bundle and ensures that future discoverability points readers to an actual falsifiable method. 02 | Three-Way Coupling of 4D Microbeam Mechanics, Quantum-Candidate Optimization and Independent Evidence The physical material changes curvature with stimulus history. An optimization policy chooses the next formulation using a limited budget; an independent measurement channel records recovery and failure. These objects are coupled only when the selected sample, fabrication recipe, instrument reading and computation cost can be separately reconstructed. Quantum-labelled optimization remains a methodological hypothesis tested against matched classical tools. Research link for F187: the controlled domain is traceable process-to-device flow with defects, missing specimens and unformed microtools. Its main independent observations are true all-input yield [1], processed specimens [h-1], failure mass fraction [1], contrasted with blocked manual inspection, classical image analysis and identical-throughput automated screening. A predeclared antagonist is excluding unformed or rejected microtools before calculating success yield; the blinded intervention is to insert coded malformed tools and count each input specimen before any downstream selection. The investigation must stop for lost sample identity, uncontained material fragment or unlogged rejection. This flagship-specific design keeps the title from being an empty keyword bundle and ensures that future discoverability points readers to an actual falsifiable method. 03 | F186–F190: Five Distinct Flagships, Five Different Ways to Fail F186 can fail through easy-batch selection or hidden computation expense. F187 can fail by eliminating malformed samples. F188 can fail by never querying rare hard formulations. F189 can fail through biased treatment allocation and hidden lot quality. F190 can fail by relabeling the same sample after software updates. Each failure requires a different witness, different denominator and different refusal. Research link for F188: the controlled domain is adaptive acquisition conditioned on unobserved recipe difficulty and sampling propensity. Its main independent observations are held-out risk [1], sample-selection coverage [1], subgroup difficulty gap [1], contrasted with stratified random sampling, classical entropy sampling and diversity-aware Bayesian selection. A predeclared antagonist is acquisition maximizing easy-case accuracy while ignoring rare difficult formulations; the blinded intervention is to blindly reweight the candidate pool after selection and evaluate unselected hard recipes separately. The investigation must stop for zero-probability candidate strata, unaccounted rejected samples or contaminated hidden labels. This flagship-specific design keeps the title from being an empty keyword bundle and ensures that future discoverability points readers to an actual falsifiable method. 04 | Thirty Formula Plates and Ninety Mechanism-Specific Scientific Annotations The candidate equations describe acquisition, all-input manufacturing yield, calibration, propensity weighting, randomized effects and provenance. Their mathematical validity as definitions does not establish a measured benefit. summary: Obesity is a growing public health issue in New Zealand, increasing the risk of chronic diseases and exacerbating health disparities. Mobile health (mHealth) initiatives, such as smartphone apps, have showed promise in improving weight management and physical exercise. FatSecret, a popular software for tracking nutrition and activity, may help people lose weight, but its efficacy across ethnic groups and areas in New Zealand is uncertain. The primary goal is to determine the efficacy of the FatSecret app in promoting weight loss and boosting physical activity among overweight and obese people in New Zealand. The secondary purpose is to investigate potential differences in intervention effectiveness based on ethnicity (European, Māori, Asian, and Pacific Islanders) and living place (urban or rural). A two-arm, parallel, randomized controlled trial design will be used. Adult volunteers (aged 18–65 years, BMI ≥25 kg/m²) from various ethnic groups and areas in New Zealand will be recruited and randomly assigned 1:1 to the intervention or control group, stratified by ethnicity and region. The intervention group will receive a 12-week weight management and physical activity program given via the FatSecret app, while the control group will not use the app and will continue with their usual lifestyle. The primary outcome is the change in body weight between baseline and 12 weeks. Secondary objectives include changes in body fat percentage, waist circumference, physical activity level measured using established methods, and health-related quality of life. This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the FatSecret app’s effectiveness in promoting weight loss and physical activity among New Zealand’s overweight and obese individuals. The study design allows for the evaluation of potential differences in intervention effectiveness across ethnic groups and residential locations, which will inform the creation of culturally appropriate and geographically targeted mHealth therapies for obesity control. If proven effective, the FatSecret app might be widely promoted and integrated into national health policies to combat the obesity pandemic and minimize health disparities. Potential limitations include self-reported data for some outcomes and the short intervention duration. Version note: Author manuscript of a study protocol prepared for DIGIHLTH 705 at the University of Auckland, listed on ResearchGate on 29 May 2025: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392166804. This is a protocol, not a report of completed trial results. This public archive copy removes the author’s student identifier and updates PDF metadata; the scientific text is otherwise unchanged.
title: Impact of the FatSecret App on Weight Management and Physical Activity among New Zealand Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol

summary: eglish version)This work presents a three-parameter mechanical-medium framework for the forward derivation of physical constants and characteristic scales within the Four-Forces–Quantum-Induction research program. The central objective is to determine how a minimal set of medium parameters can generate a hierarchy of microscopic and macroscopic physical quantities through a closed forward construction, rather than through post-hoc fitting to target observations. The current formulation includes an absolute-scale solution that no longer requires Newton’s gravitational constant as an external scale-setting calibration. Newton’s constant is instead used as a downstream consistency and round-trip closure test. The framework develops explicit relations among the characteristic medium density, elastic scale, viscosity-related input, characteristic radii, effective gravitational quantities, particle-scale structures, and derived observables. Strict NoAlias and NoDoubleCount rules are applied throughout to prevent numerically similar quantities or multiple readouts of the same physical inventory from being incorrectly identified or counted twice. An independent internal consistency test is provided by two routes to the model’s Hubble-equivalent scale. A global-field calculation and a local curvature or pressure-gradient calculation converge to approximately 67.33789544 km/s/Mpc. This quantity is reported as a model Hubble-equivalent scale. Its exact identification with the standard cosmological expansion rate H0 remains subject to a separate clock-identity condition and is therefore not assumed. The release also incorporates the current charge-conjugate electron-origin structure and the resulting birth-population asymmetry. The frozen current value is 6.117043204146319e-10. This result is treated as a theoretical output of the current model structure and is not presented as a new blind observational test. A strict theory-to-evidence firewall is maintained throughout the project. The workflow is: authority snapshot, declared inputs, forward operator, frozen prediction, external evidence, and statistical or qualitative score. Observational information is not permitted to modify a prediction after the prediction has been frozen. The empirical portfolio is intentionally reported with mixed outcomes. It includes compatible historical cross-checks, the Hubble-equivalent forward result with its explicit clock qualifier, cosmic-age consistency checks, an electron g-2 comparison that currently fails the frozen operator at high experimental precision, ring-laser results that remain retrospective rather than a new blind holdout, and prospective constant-drift predictions reserved for future evaluation. Compatible but non-discriminating tests are distinguished from genuinely discriminating evidence. The accompanying archive contains the English manuscript, validation and evidence status material, selected derivation records, Hubble-equivalent and asymmetry authority snapshots, provenance and reproducibility information, SHA256 manifests, and the sealed v4.43 historical authority package. This Zenodo release should therefore be interpreted as a frozen research record of the current theoretical construction, its absolute-scale closure, its derived cross-scale relations, and its explicitly classified empirical status. It is not a claim that every external observable has been successfully reproduced. Failed, conditional, prospective, and not-yet-opened evidence channels are retained explicitly as part of the scientific record.     预印本 — 未经同行评审。

summary: Evaluation protocol v1.0 — frozen before model implementation This release fixes the evaluation protocol of the project before any forecasting model is implemented or scored on the test period. It is archived to obtain a verifiable date for the protocol. Contents docs/PROTOCOL.md — evaluation protocol: forecast targets and horizons, information available at each issue date, models and references, metrics, the primary comparison and its statistical test, pre-specified estimates and sensitivity analyses. config/protocol.toml — machine-readable settings; the forecasting and verification code reads every analysis option from this file. Audited dataset: SOHO/LASCO CDAW catalog (version of 2026-07-31), SILSO sunspot number V2.0, and the official LASCO/C2 data-gap lists, with SHA-256 checksums and provenance ( data/raw/PROVENANCE.md , docs/data_audit.md ). Decision log ( docs/DECISIONS.md , D-01 to D-25) and tests that check the consistency of the protocol with the data. Freezing The protocol is frozen in two steps: protocol-v1.0 (this release): protocol and settings fixed before models are implemented. code-v1.0 : the code is implemented and validated on synthetic data and on data up to 2009, then tagged before the 2010–2026 test period is scored. Any later change will be recorded in docs/PROTOCOL_CHANGES.md . Exploratory analyses carried out in October 2026 had already looked at data from the test period; see the honesty note in docs/PROTOCOL.md (Section 0). Forecasts for targets after June 2026 will be verified with later catalog versions, using the code exactly as tagged.

summary: Modern AI assistants, agents, and decision-support systems increasingly rely on information beyond model parameters by retrieving documents, accessing memory, invoking tools, and combining external evidence. Retrieval-Augmented Generation is one prominent realization of this broader information-grounding paradigm. Yet external grounding does not by itself ensure trustworthiness. Systems can still fail under incomplete, noisy, conflicting, or misleading evidence, and these failures become harder to diagnose as retrieval, reasoning, memory, tool use, and generation interact. Existing evaluation frameworks measure important aspects of system quality, but do not necessarily ensure deliberate coverage of the conditions most likely to expose system vulnerabilities. We introduce PRISM as a methodology for systematic stress testing of retrieval-grounded AI through controlled synthetic data generation. Rather than treating evaluation data as a static benchmark, PRISM constructs and validates document and question-answer pairs designed to reproduce deployment-relevant failure conditions. Its 25 evaluation instruments are organized across ten diversity dimensions and eight thematic clusters, covering conditions such as fragmented or noisy evidence, lexical and semantic mismatch, unanswerable queries, and adversarial or epistemically unreliable content. Because these conditions are generated synthetically, they can reproduce relevant document and evidence characteristics without requiring access to proprietary or sensitive operational data. Stress conditions are also linked to concrete system choices to support targeted diagnosis. PRISM is expected to provide reproducible and traceable evaluation artifacts that help reveal vulnerabilities before deployment and distinguish failures originating from retrieval, evidence selection, generation, or abstention. Automated construction and validation are also intended to reduce the manual effort associated with human-curated evaluation sets while preserving the control, coverage, and consistency needed for systematic evaluation. More broadly, PRISM reframes evaluation as not only a measurement problem but also an experimental-design problem. By complementing existing metrics, human evaluation, observability, and post-deployment monitoring, it contributes toward more systematic pre-deployment assessment of increasingly agentic, retrieval-grounded AI systems.
title: Toward Trustworthy Retrieval-Grounded AI through Synthetic Stress Testing

summary: SideCow-VSS is a side-view dairy cow video semantic segmentation dataset developed to support computer vision research in precision livestock farming. The original study describes 921 five-second video clips with dense pixel-level annotations, sampled at 10 frames per second under real dairy farm conditions. The annotations were generated using a semi-automated pipeline involving YOLOv11, SAM2, and manual verification. This version (v1.0.0) provides the currently available JPEG frames and PNG segmentation annotation files, organized into the original training, validation, and testing splits. The release contains 46,024 JPEG files and 46,024 PNG files, distributed as follows: Training: 32,177 JPEG files and 32,177 PNG files. Validation: 6,897 JPEG files and 6,897 PNG files. Testing: 6,950 JPEG files and 6,950 PNG files. The dataset supports semantic segmentation of dairy cows and background regions. The original data partitions and available files are preserved without reconstructing missing frames. For details of dataset construction, annotation methodology, and benchmarking, please refer to the associated publication: Yao, L., Liu, J., Hong, W., Kong, F., Fan, Z., Lei, L., & Li, X. (2025). SideCow-VSS: A Video Semantic Segmentation Dataset and Benchmark for Intelligent Monitoring of Dairy Cows Health in Smart Ranch Environments. Veterinary Sciences , 12(11), 1104. DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/vetsci12111104

summary: This dataset is designed for comparing different algorithms for adapting a language model to the writing of a particular user. It contains the sent email messages of employees of Enron separated by user and in chronological order. We based our dataset on the Enron Personalization Validation Set released by Google and used in this CHI 2015 paper by Fowler, et al. on language model personalization. In comparison to the original dataset, our dataset provides the exact normalized text used in our experiments. We have also provided related assets such as our word list and baseline n-gram models to help facilitate future comparisons. If you use this dataset, please cite our Interspeech 2023 paper : @inproceedings{adhikary_personalization, author = {Jiban Adhikary and Keith Vertanen}, title = {Language Model Personalization for Improved Touchscreen Typing}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the International Conference on Spoken Language Processing}, location = {Dublin, Ireland}, month = {August}, year = {2023}, } This material is based upon work supported by the NSF under Grant No. IIS-1750193

summary: Configuration-driven Python pipeline (code and locked analysis plan) for the study 'Survey-design-calibrated independence tests reduce adjustment-set validity in PC-based causal discovery'. It implements design-corrected conditional-independence tests (Rao-Scott, design t test), PC-stable with temporal tiers, seven confounder-selection strategies, cross-fitted AIPW with design-based standard errors, and a simulation benchmark mimicking the 2017 Indonesia Demographic and Health Survey. IDHS microdata are not included and must be requested from The DHS Program. Release v1.1 added the deviation log (CATATAN_DEVIASI.md) and the verification scripts and reports in verifikasi/. Release v1.2 adds the exploratory strategy M7 (optimal adjustment set estimated from the M3 graph): bench_v4_m7.py and its per-replication output naskah/data/benchmark_v4/per_rep_m7.csv (4,800 replications; data and graphs identical to M0-M6), documented as a deviation in CATATAN_DEVIASI.md section 7. Release v1.3 adds the verification material for the reproducibility manuscript (verifikasi/naskah3/revisi5/): an AST-based configuration-import checker run over the git history, controlled fault injection, a BLAS thread test, bootstrap seeding schemes, a 2x2 code x configuration benchmark design with Monte Carlo intervals, and OpenTimestamps proofs for two analysis-plan manifests. The application modules causal.py, baseline.py and sol_dag.py now seed the random stream per analysis (deviation log section 8). Release v1.4 adds verification material requested in the review of the reproducibility manuscript (verifikasi/naskah3/revisi6/): detection limits of the import checker on 11 stale-import variants compared with Import Linter and a runtime guard, fault injection derived from an external configuration-error taxonomy (Yin et al., SOSP 2011), Holm correction for the 2x2 design, ULP-based floating-point differences, and an independent check of the OpenTimestamps block attestations. Import Linter is listed separately in requirements-verifikasi.txt so that the locked analysis environment is unchanged.
title: Kausal IDHS: design-based causal graph discovery and confounder selection for complex survey data

summary: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly operating over longer horizons with diminishing human oversight, raising the risk of loss of control: systems acting beyond effective human control with potentially irreversible consequences. Because such failures may become observable only after containment is difficult, they must be assessed prospectively. We introduce a behavioural framework that decomposes loss-of-control risk into three factors: misaligned motive, harm-enabling capability, and monitoring evasion. We operationalise these factors through 13 measurable aspects and 29 evaluation tasks, whose scores are combined into a single loss-of-control (LoC) score. Across 13 frontier models, the LoC score shows strong prospective validity, correlating with failure rates in contained long-horizon risk scenarios (Pearson r = 0.84). Risk varies systematically across models and cannot be explained by capability alone. We further show that the framework can guide targeted mitigations: fine-tuning and monitoring directed at diagnosed vulnerabilities reduce failure rates while largely preserving general performance. These results provide a practical basis for predicting, understanding, and mitigating loss-of-control risk before it materialises.
title: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems

summary: Tools that claim to detect emerging research topics are rarely judged on their own lists. Our main contribution is a protocol that makes such judgement possible. A bet freezes four things before its verdict can be known: the date of the photograph, the population of candidates, the verdict rule, and the comparison with chance drawn among the same candidates. The list has a fixed length, is read on two axes (champions and failures) against a computed ceiling, and is sealed by cryptographic fingerprint; sealing proves that a list existed at a date, not that it is right. A topic is a champion if its yearly volume of records triples within three years and reaches 100, a failure if it falls by 30%. We apply the protocol to one detector on PubMed/MEDLINE, in three separate blocks. On a retrospective benchmark (2017-2022), chance among the candidates yields 26.7 champions and 15.1 failures out of 120 slots; the detector yields 85 and 3, and under nine pre-registered variants of the verdict rule its champions stay between 2.5 and 5.0 times chance, with no more failures. The detector was developed with these verdicts known, and its specification is not published. Prospective validation rests on six sealed bets, judged in early 2029 and early 2030; only bets 5 and 6 test exactly the instrument of the benchmark. A secondary, exploratory study applies the same judge to eight research funders: under exact name matching, which may disadvantage grant texts, the detector's lists are more concentrated in future champions than the twenty topics named in the most grants of each funder (70.8% against 20.8% to 35.8%, chance 22.3%). We document data defects, negative results and the limits of each comparison.
title: Sealed bets on emerging research topics: a protocol for judging early detection, applied to a detector and to eight research funders

summary: Capability benchmarks measure what large language models can do, but not whether their recommendations remain appropriate as decision conditions change. This paper proposes a trajectory-based measurement framework and prospective validation protocol for artificial wisdom, defined behaviorally as context-sensitive regulation of judgment. Versioned reference specifications determine admissible responses and transition materiality before evaluation. Seven stage-level criteria assess judgment under current conditions, while two transition components assess material-update adequacy and commitment-preserving stability. Stability requires prior adequacy; switching within registered commitment classes is permitted, and persistent error earns no stability credit. A nine-component profile is primary, with a secondary bottleneck score and separate critical-failure reporting. Three simplified simulations examine precision, bottleneck estimation, and sensitivity to model-family count. A single-criterion simulation met its precision criteria at 24 scenarios per domain. Near a bottleneck tie, the estimated minimum had a downward bias of 0.55 points at that size. A simplified incremental-prediction simulation detected a Brier improvement of 0.027 with probabilities of .508 and .742 using eight and twelve families, respectively; it does not establish power for the operational protocol. An exploratory predecessor-rubric study comprising 71 evaluation records illustrates aggregation sensitivity but does not validate the proposed instrument. The twelve-family target remains provisional pending feasibility assessment and calibration of the complete analysis. Whether the profile predicts independent decision outcomes beyond capability remains an open empirical question.
title: Evaluating Artificial Wisdom (AW): A Trajectory-Based Framework for Context-Sensitive Decision Regulation

A simplified incremental-prediction simulation detected a Brier improvement of 0.027 with probabilities of .508 and .742 using eight and twelve families, respectively; it does not establish power for the operational protocol. An exploratory predecessor-rubric study comprising 71 evaluation records illustrates aggregation sensitivity but does not validate the proposed instrument. title: Evaluating Artificial Wisdom (AW): A Trajectory-Based Framework for Context-Sensitive Decision Regulation

summary: Objective: Choosing between noninvasive respiratory support (NIRS) and invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for acute respiratory failure is a time-sensitive decision. Although guidelines provide population-level guidance, it remains unclear who benefits more from NIRS than IMV. The standard outcome, ventilator-free days at 28 days (VFD-28), scores death and prolonged ventilation equally, and current estimators do not distinguish between them. We developed and validated a censoring-aware Digital Twin framework for Individualized Treatment Effects of Non-Invasive Respiratory Support (DINIRS) to estimate individualized treatment effects (ITEs) that capture both mortality and ventilation duration. Materials and Methods: We emulated a target trial in 5,336 MIMIC-IV patients and trained DINIRS on 23 baseline clinical variables measured during the first 24 ICU hours. A transformer encoder with a survival attention gate decomposed VFD-28 into survival probability and conditional ventilation duration. A cross-fitted, doubly robust learner estimated ITEs. We externally validated DINIRS in 2,540 patients from the multi-site eICU-CRD dataset without retraining. Results: The DINIRS policy achieved a mean benefit of 2.07 ventilator-free days per patient (207 per 100 patients) compared with observed practice. Predicted NIRS benefit was higher among patients with less organ dysfunction (88.4% versus 49.0%) and persisted across hypoxemia severity. External validation reproduced this pattern. Discussion: The NIRS benefit stemmed from shorter ventilation among survivors rather than from reduced mortality, indicating that avoiding intubation-associated complications was the primary mechanism. Conclusion: Prospective validation is needed before these estimates inform treatment decisions. The decomposition framework can be extended beyond respiratory support to any zero-inflated composite outcome.

summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Recent ECG foundation models offer transferable representations for automated AF detection. However, their relative effectiveness remains unclear because existing studies use different datasets, preprocessing procedures, classifiers, and validation protocols. This study presents FOUND-AF, a unified, leakage-controlled, and deployment-oriented benchmarking framework that evaluates the quality of pretrained ECG representations under identical experimental conditions. Nine publicly available foundation models from five families, including HuBERT-ECG, CLEF, ST-MEM, ECG-JEPA, and ECGFounder, were evaluated across four heterogeneous ECG datasets, namely AFDB, CinC2017, CPSC2021, and LTAFDB. All models were used as frozen feature extractors with standardized preprocessing, model-native resampling, a fixed XGBoost classifier, and recording-level grouped cross-validation. The evaluation included classification metrics, receiver operating characteristic analysis, paired recording-level bootstrap comparisons with Holm correction, embedding-space visualization, and computational efficiency profiling. The ECGFounder model consistently achieved the strongest overall performance across datasets while offering a favorable trade-off between accuracy, model size, inference time, and memory usage. FOUND-AF therefore provides a reproducible framework for selecting ECG foundation models and demonstrates that compact, clinically pretrained encoders can support robust and computationally efficient AF detection across heterogeneous acquisition settings.

summary: Large language model research agents can connect literature retrieval, analysis code, and manuscript preparation, but coherent output does not establish scientific validity. We developed Plato-Bio, a biology-routed extension of the open Plato/Denario architecture that couples explicit workflow states with provenance records, citation checks, claim-to-evidence links, scoped file writes, and publication gates. A source audit identified and repaired three defects that could distort evaluation: loss of task domain in the default factory, omission of declared method signals from scoring, and evidence sidecars that lacked the drafted-claim denominator. On the current clean revision, the full Python suite completed with 931 passes, six skips, and no failures or errors; targeted biology, genomics, evidence/citation, and adversarial-safety suites likewise completed without failure. We evaluated two narrow use cases. In a frozen historical rediscovery task, independent pre-1986 literature bridges ranked the later-studied relation between fish oil and Raynaud phenomenon first; TF-IDF ranked it second and corpus frequency third. This single curated task measures retrospective ranking, not prospective discovery. In a separate comparison of AlphaFold models with experimental structures for 15 human proteins, 11 targets had high-confidence-core C-alpha RMSD below 1 Angstrom (median 0.501 Angstrom). Four targets exceeded 2 Angstrom, and confidence masking reduced the SUMO1 discrepancy from 16.61 to 2.58 Angstrom over 74 residues. The workflow emitted 27 traceable discrepancy regions, all retained as unvalidated hypotheses. Plato-Bio therefore provides reproducible software contracts and auditable screening baselines; broader claims of agent efficacy or biological novelty require preregistered evaluation, independent review, and prospective validation.
title: Plato-Bio: verification-first biological novelty screening with temporal rediscovery and structural benchmarks

summary: Tuning of gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) is a major bottleneck for scaling spin qubit technologies. We present a deep learning (DL) driven, semantic-segmentation pipeline that performs charge auto-tuning by locating transition lines in full charge stability diagrams (CSDs) and returns gate voltage targets for the single charge regime. We assemble and manually annotate a large, heterogeneous dataset of 1015 experimental CSDs measured from silicon QD devices, spanning nine design geometries, multiple wafers, and fabrication runs. A U-Net style convolutional neural network (CNN) with a MobileNetV2 encoder is trained and validated through five-fold group cross validation. Our model achieves an overall offline tuning success of 80.0% in locating the single-charge regime, with peak performance exceeding 88% for some designs. We analyze dominant failure modes and propose targeted mitigations. Finally, wide-range diagram segmentation also naturally enables scalable physic-based feature extraction that can feed back to fabrication and design workflows and outline a roadmap for real-time integration in a cryogenic wafer prober. Overall, our results show that neural network (NN) based wide-diagram segmentation is a practical step toward automated, high-throughput charge tuning for silicon QD qubits.
title: Automatic Charge State Tuning of 300 mm FDSOI Quantum Dots Using Neural Network Segmentation of Charge Stability Diagram

summary: Camera images are ubiquitous in machine learning research. They also play a central role in the delivery of important services spanning medicine and environmental surveying. However, the application of machine learning models in these domains has been limited because of robustness concerns. A primary failure mode are performance drops due to differences between the training and deployment data. While there are methods to prospectively validate the robustness of machine learning models to such dataset drifts, existing approaches do not account for explicit models of the primary object of interest: the data. This limits our ability to study and understand the relationship between data generation and downstream machine learning model performance in a physically accurate manner. In this study, we demonstrate how to overcome this limitation by pairing traditional machine learning with physical optics to obtain explicit and differentiable data models. We demonstrate how such data models can be constructed for image data and used to control downstream machine learning model performance related to dataset drift. The findings are distilled into three applications. First, drift synthesis enables the controlled generation of physically faithful drift test cases to power model selection and targeted generalization. Second, the gradient connection between machine learning task model and data model allows advanced, precise tolerancing of task model sensitivity to changes in the data generation. These drift forensics can be used to precisely specify the acceptable data environments in which a task model may be run. Third, drift optimization opens up the possibility to create drifts that can help the task model learn better faster, effectively optimizing the data generating process itself. A guide to access the open code and datasets is available at https://github.com/aiaudit-org/raw2logit.
title: Data Models for Dataset Drift Controls in Machine Learning With Optical Images

summary: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits. Two benchmarking findings explain why this went unnoticed. The standard CIRCLE-seq file lists ten guides under eighty on-target strings, so grouping cross-validation on the sequence column trains and tests on one guide; corrected, pair-level discrimination and per-guide fidelity collapse. With that leakage removed, a training-free position-weight score and a bare count of near-match genomic sites are not beaten by a trained oracle. We give the corrected protocol, the baselines a new model must beat, and the cohort size a certified pipeline needs.
title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement

summary: Acoustic indices are widely used as rapid proxies for biodiversity, but they summarise the distribution of sound energy rather than the species producing it and often track richness poorly. We revise and test an Acoustic Biodiversity Index (ABI) built from species-level detections. Its primary form, ABI_E, is Shannon diversity of detections normalised by the regional species pool expected at the site and season (H / ln S_ref); temporal stability T is reported as a separate component. We first benchmarked four classifiers on a strongly labelled tropical dataset (1,216 calls, 24 classes) with recording-grouped cross-validation. BirdNET embeddings + logistic regression performed best (macro-F1 0.750 +/- 0.029), and random frame-level splits inflated accuracy from 0.41 to 0.70. We then applied BirdNET v2.4 with a location and season filter to recordings from a riverine savanna in the Zambezi Valley, Zimbabwe, and from three habitats at Emirates Park Zoo and Resort, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. A stricter post-hoc location filter removed 517 high-confidence detections of 9 implausible species, all at the zoo. After diel-matched rarefaction to equal effort (6 h), the savanna site held 21 species (Hill number 1D = 9.83; ABI_E = 0.38) against 1.3-13 species (ABI_E = 0.03-0.21) at the zoo sites. Across 149 recorded hours, ABI_E correlated strongly with richness (Spearman rho = 0.93), whereas six standard indices did not (best: ACI, rho = 0.48). The stability term was lower at the savanna site (0.39) than at the zoo (0.65-0.67), showing that it penalises the natural diel cycle of bird activity. Species-level indices with explicit false-positive control, a declared regional reference pool and effort standardisation provide a more interpretable biodiversity indicator than energy-based acoustic indices.
title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can benefit from more sophisticated retrieval, but extra retrieval may be unnecessary for many questions and gains in evidence retrieval may not translate into faithful or correct answers. We study a cost-aware, two-action retrieval policy that chooses between a dense-retrieval-plus-reranking baseline and a hybrid lexical--dense retriever. Rather than classifying baseline retrieval as simply successful or unsuccessful, we estimate the question-specific incremental evidence-retrieval benefit of hybrid retrieval using features available before the routing decision. A regularized linear model and decision threshold are selected using document-grouped cross-validation and frozen prior to held-out evaluation. On 60 previously unseen QASPER training-split articles (188 questions, 169 evidence-evaluable), the policy triggers hybrid retrieval on 46 questions (24.5\%) and obtains the same evidence Hit@10 as always-hybrid retrieval (78.70\%, versus 76.92\% for always-keep). Paired, paper-cluster bootstrap intervals do not establish a reliable utility advantage. We further compare generated answers from a 4-bit Qwen3-4B model under the three retrieval policies. Provisional answer-level assessments show no clear correctness or faithfulness improvement after partial review, despite the evidence-retrieval result. The generation assessments remain model-assisted and lack independent human validation. These results expose an important distinction between retrieving relevant evidence efficiently and improving the reliability of the generated answer. The work is presented as a reproducible empirical study, not a claim of statistically established answer-quality superiority.
title: When Is Additional Retrieval Worthwhile? A Cost-Aware Study of Evidence Gain and Answer Reliability in RAG
